threads.body: [General] Rebuilding from `Context.root()` drops the global `InstrumentationUtil` suppression key. A raw poll wrapped in `InstrumentationUtil.suppressInstrumentation(...)` inside a Spring listener will therefore emit a receive span because `shouldStart` is evaluated against this stripped context. Preserve or explicitly check global instrumentation suppression while bypassing only the framework process-span suppression.

replies.body:
Addressed in 31d84e8449f7abc21e7ebd3a6d2b5d120c2562b4.

Analysis: The framework-specific context rebuild must not run when the parent context carries global instrumentation suppression. Returning that context unchanged lets the instrumenter's standard suppressor prevent the receive span. A focused unit test reproduces the suppression loss.

Upsides: Raw Kafka polls remain fully suppressed when application code requests global suppression, including inside a Spring listener.

Downsides: The bootstrap helper performs one extra suppression-key lookup when it sees the Spring framework marker. The unit test needs explicit OpenTelemetry API and javaagent bootstrap dependencies.

threads.body: [Style] This overload is only called by `AbstractMessageListenerContainerInstrumentation` in the same package, so making it public unnecessarily adds an agent-only customization hook to the Spring Kafka library API. Keep it package-private.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: `SpringKafkaTelemetry` is in `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.spring.kafka.v2_7`, while `AbstractMessageListenerContainerInstrumentation` is in `io.opentelemetry.javaagent.instrumentation.spring.kafka.v2_7`. Package-private access cannot cross that package boundary, so the suggested modifier would break the javaagent caller.

Upsides: Keeping the overload public preserves the direct, type-safe call between the javaagent and library modules without adding a bridge solely to hide this method.

Downsides: The agent-only overload remains visible on the library class.

threads.body: [Testing] The new raw-consumer regression test exercises only the record-interceptor path, while batch listeners reach this independent advice path. Add a batch-listener case that polls and iterates a raw consumer and verifies exactly one nested receive/process operation so this ownership marker and batch claim are covered.

replies.body:
Addressed in cf6183eec1f4c92afbf4679a7fe5696ecf1d676e.

Analysis: The batch listener reaches ListenerConsumerInstrumentation instead of the record interceptor. A dedicated callback now runs the same raw poll-and-iterate scenario from the batch listener against a separate topic, and the test asserts exactly one nested receive span and one nested process span.

Upsides: The independent batch ownership and claim path now has regression coverage in the default and messaging semantic convention test variants.

Downsides: The integration test adds one Kafka topic and another listener callback hook, which modestly increases test runtime and fixture state.
